title: Why interface default methods do not imply instance fields
answer: A default method is inheritable behavior, but an interface still does not own ordinary per-object instance state. Fields declared in an interface are implicitly public static final constants. Allowing mutable instance fields would require interface-defined object layout, construction, and state ownership, which would conflict with unrelated classes implementing the same contract while managing their own state.
